bull.b: Reported debt is only about $9K against $1.36M of TTM equity, limiting direct interest and leverage pressure in the near term. This gives the company some balance-sheet flexibility while it funds development, although it does not offset severe cash burn.

Combining with Redx would broaden Skye beyond its current metabolic focus into fibrotic disease, while the proposed Fibrx platform includes a Phase 2 lead asset and broader pipeline. If completed, this could improve program diversification and milestone potential.

The proposed financing package would provide substantial capital for clinical development and key milestones through 2029. That funding could reduce near-term financing pressure and support execution of the combined company’s pipeline, although operations remain externally funded.

bear.b: Zero revenue and large recurring losses show the company has not yet commercialized a product or established an operating earnings base. Losses rose from about $26.6M in 2024 to $55.9M in 2025 and remained elevated TTM, leaving profitability dependent on successful development.

Operating and free cash flow remain negative in every period, with TTM burn around $30.6M. Because operations are not self-funding, continued clinical development and corporate activity depend heavily on external capital, making liquidity and financing execution central to the outlook.

Negative stockholders’ equity of $497,307 at June 30, 2026 breached Nasdaq’s $2.5M requirement and creates a continuing compliance overhang. Remediation efforts and possible delisting could disrupt exchange access and complicate the Redx transaction and future financing.
